documents.title: Fictional Case: Termination for Convenience
documents.text:
FICTIONAL TRAINING MATERIAL — NOT REAL LAW.

SECTION 4.2 Termination for Convenience
Either party may terminate this agreement for convenience by providing the other party with thirty days' prior written notice. The notice must be delivered to the addresses designated in the agreement.

documents.title: Fictional Case: Written Contract Limitation Period
documents.text:
FICTIONAL TRAINING MATERIAL — NOT REAL LAW.

SECTION 12.1 Limitation Period for Contract Claims
An action for breach of a written contract must be filed within six years after the claim accrues. The parties cannot shorten this period by informal correspondence.

documents.title: Fictional Case: Survival of Confidentiality Duties
documents.text:
FICTIONAL TRAINING MATERIAL — NOT REAL LAW.

SECTION 8.4 Continuing Confidentiality Obligations
The confidentiality obligations in this agreement continue for five years after termination. Trade secrets remain protected for as long as they qualify as trade secrets under the agreement.

documents.title: Fictional Case: Emergency Injunctive Relief
documents.text:
FICTIONAL TRAINING MATERIAL — NOT REAL LAW.

SECTION 15.2 Emergency Relief
A party may seek temporary injunctive relief from a court of competent jurisdiction to prevent irreparable harm. Seeking such relief does not waive other remedies.
